explanation: The `case 'gold':` branch is missing a `break` statement, so execution falls through into `case 'silver':` and overwrites `discount` with 10 instead of stopping at 20. Gold-tier customers end up receiving the silver discount rate.
prompt: What's the bug in this discount calculator?
choices: Missing `break` after `case 'gold':` causes fall-through into the 'silver' case, so gold customers get a 10% discount instead of 20%
The `default` case should come before the other cases
`discount` should be declared with `const` instead of `let`
The function should use `if/else` instead of `switch` because strings can't be compared with `case`
